comment: Every role the package disagrees with, and what was decided about it.
Exact equality, not a ratchet down: a new disagreement and a resolved one both fail, because both
are a decision somebody has to record. Re-bank deliberately with UPDATE_ROLES_BASELINE=1 pnpm test,
and fill in the decision - a banked entry without one fails too.
verdict   cross-family   - the package uses this role, but only for a slot of another kind
family-conflict - the package paints this slot from another family entirely
decision  confirmed   - the package assigns this very role here; only our slot word differs
naming      - the role is right for what the property paints; the slot word is not
rule-5      - one value in two roles, named after the dominant one (DIVERGENCES)
bridge      - built with rgb(from role / a); the foundation names no role for it
package-gap - no role of the right family exists; a request, not a swap
design      - a correction would move a pixel, so it is not ours to make
typographyUnmarked - typography step reads that carry no marker at all. The px gate only looks at
literals, so a step read slipped past it; these are banked until each one is routed to a role or
marked with a reason.
slotLies - the slot word contradicts the CSS property the bundle shows it painting. Same rules as
above: banked with a decision, exact equality. hairline and rule-5 are deliberate and stay; naming
is a rename wave waiting for a changelog, not a role defect.
ladders - a slot whose states resolve to one role. `focused` reusing `hovered` is accepted
convention and never listed. decision no-rung means the system has no role for the second state
either; design means it does and we skip it.
contrast - foreground and background the bundle puts in ONE rule, resolved per mode. Alpha-bridge
values and disabled selectors are excluded: the first renders as a tint over an unknown surface,
the second is exempt from WCAG 1.4.3 and gated by disabled-paint.test.ts. decision graphic-ok means
the pair is a glyph and clears 3:1; design means it misses the threshold that applies to it.
concepts - one anatomical concept (modifiers + slot + state, sub-elements dropped) painted with
several roles across components. This is the only check that asks the question the task is named
after; every other one reads a single declaration. decision spelling means the roles resolve to one
colour and differ only in family, shade means same family different value, design means the
components disagree about the colour itself.
judgmentCalls - where the decision was not read off the package or a standard. Kept because a
fixed item leaves the lists above and its reasoning would leave with it.

Re-read 14.09 after being asked whether the accordion answer transfers and whether cardView holds the answer. It does not transfer, and the row was reading one slot instead of the element. The tile IS laddered, just not on the background: rest is color-bg with a color-border-subtle edge, hover and focus keep the same background and move the edge to color-border-primary, and the pressed state tints with color-bg-alpha-active and drops the edge to transparent. So the hover cue is the border, the flat background is deliberate, and the pressed state is already on the very alpha role the accordion has just adopted. cardView offers no counter-example: its card has no hover rule at all, and its header panel item uses a third idiom, bg-low to bg-low-hovered. What is left is a smaller, real defect: $tile-view-bg-hovered exists only to restate the rest value, so it is a name that promises a state and delivers none. Options: (1) delete it and the background-color line in the hover rule - value-neutral, one fewer public name, and it records that the cue is the border; (2) follow the accordion and give it bg-alpha-hovered, so the tile gains a tint on top of the border cue - a pixel change and an etalon re-shoot. Recommendation: (1), unless design wants the tile to feel like the accordion.

contrast.why: WRONG, corrected 09.09. The 3.36 is the rest state and nothing else, because the pass that produced it can only measure a foreground and a background written in one rule. One keystroke away the same element reads 1.62: the focused and active rules repaint the fill and leave the checkmark to the rest rule, so the pair is split across rules and was invisible. See statePairs and the group checkbox-focused-fill. Kept listed so the rest state is still watched, but the graphic-ok verdict now belongs to the rest state only.
the attention mark is a glyph on the invalid disc: 3.68 clears 3:1. Same reason to keep it listed

Widened 09.09 after asking whether danger passes anywhere else. It does not, and the reason is that the role is tuned to one surface. In dark content-danger is danger-80 #e4554f, and it measures 4.58 on the page canvas (bg-canvas #1d1d1d), 4.22 on an ordinary surface (bg #242424) and 3.05 on a hovered one (bg-hovered #3b3b3b). So it clears AA on the canvas by 0.08 and fails everywhere below it. Eleven theme variables put real text on this role - the outlined danger button label, the chat alert list, the chat delete item, the fieldset invalid value, the grid AI error, the informer error, two stepper invalid labels, the text editor invalid message, the validation message and the validation summary - and every one of them sits at 4.22 wherever its widget has its own background. Three more read the role for a glyph (diagram, filterBuilder, cardView), where 4.22 clears the 3:1 that applies. The request splits in two: on an ordinary surface the miss is 0.28 and one ramp step fixes it - danger-70 #ee726a gives 5.36 - so ask the package to move content-danger in dark; on a hovered surface nothing in the family clears AA, danger-70 reaching only 3.87, so that half is a genuine gap. Light is fine throughout (6.07 on the canvas, 5.56 hovered). Why the audit saw one row and not twelve: the rule-local pass needs both colours in one rule, and a validation message takes its background from an ancestor. Third instance of that blind spot in one day.

Revised 09.09. Blazor sets splitter-resize-handle-color to content-subtle - our role exactly - so the grip is not an anomaly and there is nothing to swap it for on consistency grounds. The 2.8 in dark stands as an observation against the 3:1 floor. The wider claim this row grew into needs a qualifier: the bar is invisible in light at 1.62, but Blazor paints the same bar with bg-canvas, which is 1.04 against a pane - worse than ours. Every product in the family has an unidentifiable splitter in light, so this is a design-system question, not a defect of this theme.

Answered 09.09, and the answer is not to unify. Measured: the whole *-danger-shared family resolves to ONE value across bg, border and content in both modes - that is what shared means in this set. So the family segment carries no colour information here; it records which property paints the value. The canonical spelling is therefore already decided by the theme's own slot rule (NAMING M3, family follows the painted property), and unifying the three would throw away the only information the segment carries. If the package ever diverges the three, each element will then correctly follow its own family - which is the outcome the original worry asked for. Every member of the cluster already obeys the rule: checkBox border paints border-color, checkBox fill paints background-color, checkBox mark is a glyph, common badge is a fill. The one exception is radioButton, which paints a border AND a fill from a single variable - that is not a spelling choice, it is the anatomy question filed as sweep:radio-invalid-vs-checkbox-invalid. All three roles here resolve to one colour (#76000b light / #9d0013 dark), so this row is a pure spelling cluster and nothing else.

Компоненты у WPF есть (Gantt 12 xaml, Diagram 14, RichEdit 8), но их темы НЕ затокенизированы: семантические ключи вида AccordionHeaderBackgroundRest получают только компоненты из components/wpf, а Gantt и Diagram красятся легаси-палитрой Lightweight, где Color.Foreground.Primary — это литерал #FF1A1A1A. Зато Lightweight/Common/PaletteSemantics.md описывает смысл 142 ключей словами («Color.Border — primary border brush for controls»). Это сигнал уровня семейства (border / bg / content), а не роли, и он покрывает ровно то, чего нет больше нигде: gantt 14, diagram 20, htmlEditor 13.

Но одними словами они описывают почти ничего: у button 401 путь анатомии на четыре продукта и ноль общих для всех четырёх. comment: Why a contrast pair below AA does not turn the dark a11y job red. Asked 09.09.2026 and grounded
in axe-core 4.12.1 source rather than assumed - the answer is structural, so it applies to every
future finding of the same shape.

reasons.reason: axe reads DOM text nodes, and an icon glyph is not one
reasons.detail: visibleTextNodes() in axe-core collects children with nodeType === 3. DevExtreme icon fonts render through ::before { content: "\fXXX" }, which is generated content, not a child node - so an element whose only text is a glyph never enters the color-contrast rule. The splitter grip is exactly that: dx-icon-sizing sets a font-size on .dx-resize-handle-icon and the glyph arrives from the icon font.
reasons.covers: every chevron, checkmark, arrow, grip and spinner in the theme

reasons.reason: WCAG 1.4.11 has no axe rule at all
reasons.detail: Non-text contrast - 3:1 for control boundaries and graphics - is not implemented in axe. Borders, focus rings, indicators and switch tracks are outside the gate by construction, not by suppression.
reasons.covers: the whole non-text half of the contrast requirement

reasons.reason: the state has to be reached
reasons.detail: The delete item in the message-list context menu measures 3.05 in dark, and it is real text - but only while the menu is open and that item focused. A pair that needs a state the a11y suite never enters is invisible even when the rule applies to it.
reasons.covers: findings in transient states: focused, opened, invalid

comment: Contrast measured across a state change - added 09.09.2026, and it is what the rest of this file
could not see. The rule-local pass needs a foreground and a background in one rule; a state
ladder never writes them together, so the states where a value actually moves were exactly the
blind spot. Exact equality: a row leaving or entering this list is a decision, not a ratchet.
threshold: 4.5 where the foreground is a label, 3 where it is a glyph or a boundary (WCAG 1.4.11).

checkbox-focused-fill.why: The checked checkbox, focused or pressed, fills with bg-primary-active and keeps its checkmark on content-inverted. Those two roles behave differently across modes: content-inverted flips (#ffffff light, #161616 dark), bg-primary-active does not (#003c70 in both). Light gets 11.17, dark gets 1.62 - the mark is gone, and the box itself is 1.39 against the page. The rest state is 3.36 and the hovered state 4.30, so only this rung fails. Measured alternatives for the fill in dark, mark first, box second: bg-primary-hovered #2b7ecf 4.30 / 3.69 (passes, and it is the rung the contained button already uses for focus - see button/_colors.scss, bg-focused reads bg-primary-hovered); bg-primary-shared-active #005397 2.31 / 1.98 (still fails, so the Д3 move does not transfer here); leaving it 1.62 / 1.39. Recommendation: bg-primary-hovered, which makes the checkbox agree with the button. Light moves 11.17 -> 7.82 and the fill goes #003c70 -> #005397, so etalons need re-shooting - that is why it is a question and not applied.

outlined-button-label.why: The outlined buttons - default, success, danger - hold their label on content-<hue> while the fill climbs bg-<hue>-subtler through hovered, focused, selected and active. The label is text, so the floor is 4.5, and no state after rest reaches it: hover and focus 4.02-4.43, selected 3.22-3.78, active 2.94-3.18 in light. Blazor climbs both sides - outline-primary-hover-color is content-primary-hovered and -active-color is content-primary-active - and measuring its pairing answers the question unevenly: content-primary-hovered on bg-primary-subtler-hovered gives 5.85 light / 5.11 dark, which clears AA in both and is a straight improvement on our 4.02 / 4.11; but content-primary-active on bg-primary-subtler-active gives 6.10 light / 2.05 dark, trading one mode for the other, and content-primary-selected does not exist at all. So: (1) adopt Blazor's hovered and focused rungs - provable, both modes, three roles; (2) for selected and active there is no shipped pair that passes, so either hold the fill still in those states or ask the package; (3) content-on-subtle-primary, which the package ships for exactly this surface and we never read, clears everything by a mile (10.82 / 16) but is neutral, not blue - it would stop the label being an accent. Recommendation: (1) now, (3) only if design wants a neutral label.

contained-button-label.why: The filled default and success buttons, and the completed stepper indicator, put a white label on bg-<hue>-hovered and land at 4.18-4.21 in dark against the 4.5 a label needs. Light is 7.5-7.8, so this is dark-only. The foreground is content-static-dark, which is #ffffff in both modes by design, so the whole movement is in the fill: bg-primary in dark is #0f6cbd giving 5.38, and its hovered rung lightens to #2b7ecf giving 4.21. A hover that lightens is correct for dark; it is the amount that overshoots. Nothing in the theme can fix this - the pair is two package roles used exactly as intended - so this is a report to the design system, alongside the danger-content row already filed. Listed as a question only to confirm we file it rather than swap a role.

items.title: scheduler: две силы линии сетки на одной роли - принято
items.why: Answered 14.09: if both lines are meant to be the same colour then two variables reading one role is fine, and the collapse is deliberate rather than a loss. Recorded so the audit does not reopen it. Worth noting what is NOT a problem here: the word accent in $scheduler-accent-border comes from the base layer, which names the parameter $scheduler-accent-border-color, and the theme takes its anatomy from base (NAMING M1). So the name is not lying about the theme - it is repeating the anatomy the markup already draws, which still has two lines even when they share a colour. Both variables stay: base needs two parameters, and a future theme may want them apart, as generic already does with 60% alpha against a 10% darkened edge.

items.title: scheduler: иконки формы встречи красятся bg-ролью, 1.56 в светлом
items.why: The appointment form paints .dx-scheduler-form-subject-group .dx-scheduler-form-icon with --dx-scheduler-appointment-base-content, which reads bg-primary-subtle. In light that is primary-40 #b4d2f4 on the popup background #ffffff: 1.56 against the 3:1 a glyph needs. The role itself is right for what the variable mostly does - Blazor names the same role default-appointment-background-color, so bg-primary-subtle IS the appointment fill - but this variable is read by four different things: the appointment fill, the appointment marker, the focused-cell inset ring, and this icon. Legacy fluent does the same (the form icon takes $scheduler-appointment-base-color, accent lightened 48%), so NFR-1 protects the pixel and this is a report, not a fix. Options: (1) leave it, legacy parity; (2) split the icon off onto content-primary, which is 5.38 light / 4.65 dark, and accept a visible change in the appointment form; (3) split it off and keep the pale tint, which fixes the name but not the contrast. Recommendation: (2) if the form is meant to be usable, (1) if legacy parity outranks it - this one is genuinely a product call.

items.title: Кольцо и заливка мелкого контрола: одна анатомия, четыре решения
items.why: Widened 09.09 when category Г was taken to the end. It started as radio versus checkbox and it is bigger: four controls paint the same anatomy - the ring of a small control plus its fill - and each resolves it differently. The checkbox splits it in two, border role on the ring and content role on the mark. The radio paints both from one variable on a border role but calls the variable bg. The read-only radio paints both from one variable on a CONTENT role, though no property is text. The slider does it twice with roles from different families - accent focused on a bg role, invalid focused on a border role - for the identical pair of properties. The treeView checkbox does it on a bg role and follows its own question. Nothing here is about pixels: the whole *-danger-shared family resolves to one value across bg, border and content in both modes. It is about which anatomy the family agrees on. Splitting is not free in code either - the radio rest-state variable is a parameter of dx-radiobutton-states-mixin in base, so splitting it changes a base signature and touches generic and material. Options: (1) adopt the checkbox shape everywhere, correct anatomy, costs a base parameter; (2) keep one variable per control but name and role it by the ring, which is the part always drawn, so the fill borrows a border role openly; (3) leave the four as they are and record the divergence. Recommendation: (2) now, since it is theme-local and value-neutral, and (1) whenever the base is opened for other reasons.

items.title: treeView всё ещё красит чекбокс по-своему в фокусе элемента
items.why: The disabled overrides are gone. The focus block is not: when the treeView ITEM has focus, the checkbox inside it is repainted with three values of its own (treeView/_index.scss:18-72). They are not the checkbox own focus values: unchecked border goes to color-border where the checkbox uses bg-primary-active, unchecked fill goes to bg-low where the checkbox sets none, and the checked fill goes to bg-primary-hovered where the checkbox uses bg-primary-active. So three distinct divergences remain, and the rule stated for this widget - no unique checkbox styling in treeView - is not yet met. Removing the block is NOT value-neutral, which is why it was not done with the disabled one: legacy fluent carries the same block, so the pixel is inherited, not invented. There is a real argument for removing it beyond tidiness: the checkbox itself is not focused here, the item is, so painting the checkbox as focused states something untrue to a keyboard user. Options: (1) remove the block - the checkbox stops reacting to item focus, three variables and one public name go, etalons re-shoot; (2) keep the block but point its three values at the checkbox own focus roles, so treeView adds no roles of its own - still a pixel change, smaller; (3) keep as is for legacy parity. Note that (1) and (2) both collide with the checkbox-focused-fill question: whatever the checkbox focus fill becomes, this follows it. Recommendation: settle checkbox-focused-fill first, then (1).

comment: Каждый вердикт - в одну и только одну секцию страницы. Таблица «решения не требуется» строится
отсюда и считается по данным: раньше это был литеральный массив в генераторе, и он уже разошёлся
с данными - graphic-ok печатался как 2, когда строк было 1, а graphic-ok-rest-only не попадал
никуда вовсе. Гейт держит равенство в обе стороны: вердикт без класса и класс без строк роняют
проверку, и сумма по секциям обязана сойтись с числом разобранных строк.
Класс заводится только когда строка с таким вердиктом есть в данных: пустой класс роняет гейт так
же, как неотнесённый вердикт. Поэтому spelling здесь нет - все три строки отвечены (answered).

Не метрика, а страж: каждая проверка, которая смотрит на красящее свойство, ЗАМОЛКАЕТ, если
бандл старше исходников - переименованная переменная просто не находится, свойства у неё нет,
